title: Dockerfile.ci odin-locate pipeline lacks the workflow's `|| true`; the designed empty-result diagnostic is unreachable under set -euo pipefail
evidence: Dockerfile.ci line 39: `RUN set -euo pipefail \`; line 50: `&& ODIN_BIN="$(find /opt/odin -maxdepth 3 -name odin -type f | head -1 | xargs dirname)" \`; lines 51-53: `&& if [ -z "${ODIN_BIN:-}" ] || [ ! -x "$ODIN_BIN/odin" ]; then \` `     echo "odin binary not found; artifact layout:"; find /opt/odin -maxdepth 3 | head -20; exit 1; \` — vs the workflow it mirrors, ci.yml: `ODIN_BIN="$(find "$RUNNER_TEMP/odin" -maxdepth 3 -name odin -type f | head -1 | xargs dirname || true)"`
detail: Empty find result makes xargs run dirname with no args (exit 1); pipefail + set -e abort the RUN before the empty-check guard, so the 'odin binary not found' layout dump never prints on a corrupt/empty tarball.
recommended_fix: Mirror the workflow: append `|| true` to the find|head|xargs pipeline so an empty result reaches the existing [ -z ] guard and prints the layout dump.

title: README gate-mapping table covers 9 of the workflow's 11 non-checkout steps as rows
evidence: README.md lines 70-80: `| GH CI step | Local stage |` ... `| Upload diff bundles on failure | `goldens/_reports/` (bind-mounted out of the container) |` (9 rows total; the two setup steps appear only in prose at lines 61-64: "it installs the pinned Odin release tarball exactly like the workflow's `Install Odin` step ... the workflow's X11 link deps") — vs ci.yml step names `- name: Install Odin (pinned release artifact)` and `- name: Linux GUI link deps`; spec task claimed "gate-mapping table (all 11 workflow steps)"
detail: The table omits 'Install Odin (pinned release artifact)' and 'Linux GUI link deps' as rows (prose-only), so the table does not map the workflow 1:1 as the lens guard and spec task require.
recommended_fix: Add the two setup steps as rows: 'Install Odin (pinned release artifact) | Dockerfile.ci lines 39-55' and 'Linux GUI link deps | Dockerfile.ci lines 27-32'.

title: README x64-parity recipe (`docker run --platform linux/amd64`) bypasses the --user/--rm bind-mount, losing the host report surface
evidence: README.md lines 100-104: "but to replicate the x64 runner leg exactly: `docker build --platform linux/amd64` + `docker run --platform linux/amd64` (emulated; slower)." — the raw docker run executes Dockerfile.ci's CMD (`CMD ["tools/ci-local.sh", "--in-container"]`) without the mount/user wiring that only ci-local.sh applies (tools/ci-local.sh lines 195-198: `docker run --rm \` `--user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \` `-v "$reports:/src/goldens/_reports" \`)
detail: The documented parity flow runs the image as root with no goldens/_reports mount and no --rm; failure bundles land root-owned in a left-behind container, contradicting the README's 'only writable host surface' guarantee for that flow.
recommended_fix: Show the parity flow through ci-local.sh (e.g. DOCKER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM=linux/amd64 tools/ci-local.sh) or document the full docker run with -v and --user.

title: Empty .odin-version passes the readability guard: false toolchain warning natively, misattributed curl 404 in the container
evidence: tools/ci-local.sh lines 139-143: `if [ ! -r .odin-version ]; then` `echo "ERROR: .odin-version is missing or unreadable — cannot verify the toolchain pin" >&2` `exit 1` `fi` `pin="$(cat .odin-version)"` — no emptiness check; Dockerfile.ci line 47: `&& curl -fsSL "https://github.com/odin-lang/Odin/releases/download/${PIN}/${ASSET}" -o /tmp/odin.tar.gz \` (empty PIN -> double-slash URL); tools/ci-local.sh line 173: "ERROR: docker build failed — check the output above (network fetch of the pinned toolchain is the usual cause)."
detail: Only readability is guarded, not the value: an empty pin emits a false-positive toolchain warning in native mode (token != ""), and in-container fails at curl with the cause blamed on network rather than the empty pin.
recommended_fix: Validate the pin is non-empty after reading it in both run_native and the Dockerfile RUN, with an error naming .odin-version as the cause.

title: `--windows-cross --in-container` on the host passes both conflict checks; success message falsely claims the container discarded app-win.exe
evidence: tools/ci-local.sh lines 209-216: conflict checks cover only `[ "$WIN_CROSS" -eq 1 ] && [ "$FAST" -eq 1 ]` and `[ "$IN_CONTAINER" -eq 1 ] && [ "$NATIVE" -eq 1 ]`; lines 220-222 dispatch `if [ "$WIN_CROSS" -eq 1 ]; then run_windows_cross; exit $?; fi` before the IN_CONTAINER branch; lines 116-121: `if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ -s app-win.exe ]; then` `if [ "$IN_CONTAINER" -eq 1 ]; then` `echo "   ✅ windows_amd64 cross-build succeeded → app-win.exe (in-container; the --rm container discards it)"`
detail: Run on the host, the pair probes the host toolchain and a successful build prints the in-container message while app-win.exe persists in the host tree; the pair is only legitimately generated inside the container (line 198).
recommended_fix: Drop the IN_CONTAINER-dependent wording from the success message, or reject the pair on the host since --in-container is undocumented in usage().
